The office location (for where we live) is a plus! The price was reasonable. Technician/nurse Megan was nice & warm as this was our puppy’s first time there. The staff were apologetic running behind due to needing to sanitize the room and have it dry. The attending vet didn’t introduce herself, offered little eye contact. I don’t remember a single question of us regarding the puppy’s well-being. Vet seemed more interested typing a couple notes in the computer and recommended shots every three weeks than anything. The best thing she did was give the shot without a hitch and catch the start of an ear infection. I asked about getting the next shot in four weeks from then and she just told me “no in three weeks” without any rationale or reasoning behind it. Also, she recommend a fourth Canine parvovirus vaccine shot, which is not going to happen, as the typical recommendation has always been three parvovirus shots total. I get that it was busy on a Monday, but still the bedside manners was nothing to be desired. Last but not least, having the fingernails clipped by the last technician. I wasn’t expecting it to be super pleasant, but the technician was not paying close attention and the first one was clipped slightly into her skin, and she verbally reprimanded puppy to do better (when I was holding her and trying to make it the best first nail clipping experience possible). We went there because they were close and the reviews are mostly high. Now I am scratching my head how they managed to have 4.9 stars? The only reason why I filled out this review is because they have an automatic email requesting reviews on Google and FB, so this is my honest experience. Even my 10-year-old was not impressed from start to finish. Maybe a different day and a different Dr would’ve affected that but we will not be back.

I am writing this review after taking some time to process what happened, because I wanted to be fair and keep emotion out of my words as much as possible.
I recently brought my 16-year-old dog, Mia, to this clinic in an emergency situation. She had suddenly become blind, was unable to walk, and was in extremely serious condition. I had her wrapped in a blanket and carried her into the clinic from the parking lot. At that point, she was barely responsive. My own doctor had even told me that she would pay whatever was necessary to help me get answers and assistance for Mia.
I understand that veterinary clinics have appointments, surgeries, and emergencies of their own. I understand that a clinic may not be able to immediately see a patient who walks in without an appointment. I was not expecting the staff to simply cancel another patient’s appointment or stop a surgery.
What I was expecting was basic compassion and some kind of guidance.
As I walked in carrying my dog, the front office staff member was already shaking her head no before I had even finished explaining why I was there. I was visibly crying and struggling to speak. I was told that I would need an appointment, that it might not be available for quite some time, possibly the following week, and that the veterinarian was in surgery. I was told I would need to take Mia somewhere else.
I understand that they may not have been able to examine her. What I found deeply upsetting was the complete lack of compassion or assistance in that moment. When I asked if there was any information they could provide or anything I could do to help keep my dog comfortable while I found another veterinarian, I did not receive an answer. I was simply met with another shake of the head.
I was not asking for special treatment. I was asking for help finding help.
Even if the clinic could not see Mia, I believe the situation could have been handled very differently. A simple expression of concern, an apology that they could not accommodate her, or even a referral to an emergency clinic or some basic guidance would have meant a great deal.
Mia passed away shortly afterward.
I understand policies and scheduling limitations. What I will never understand is how someone can see a person carrying a nearly lifeless, 16-year-old dog into a veterinary clinic while sobbing and offer absolutely no compassion, assistance, or direction.
I hope this clinic considers training its front office staff on how to respond to people experiencing an animal emergency. Sometimes you may not be able to treat the animal—but you can still show kindness and help the person find somewhere that can.

I brought my foster cat here to get spayed and they did a wonderful job taking care of her. They communicated to me when she was done with surgery and when she was ready for pick up.

I would not recommend North Phoenix Animal Clinic based on our experience.

We scheduled our dog’s spay surgery after she had been in heat. When we called, we were specifically advised to wait until her cycle was completely over because her uterus could be inflamed during that time. The staff recommended scheduling her surgery for June 29th and told us that she should be finished with her cycle by then. We followed their recommendation and scheduled the procedure on the date they provided.

After the surgery, we were charged an additional fee because they claimed she was still in heat and that her uterus was enlarged. This was extremely frustrating because we did exactly what their staff instructed us to do. If the timing they recommended was not appropriate, that should have been communicated before the surgery—not used as a reason to add unexpected charges afterward.

We also felt pressured throughout the process with multiple recommended add-ons. Even after declining certain items, the technician continued adding them to the chart as “highly recommended.” One example was a catheter. When I asked if it was only necessary if something went wrong, I was told yes. I declined that charge because it seemed unnecessary, especially since they would have the ability to handle an emergency situation if one occurred.

We did agree to pay for a nail trim, but when we brought our dog home, we noticed her nails had not been trimmed.

This was not our first visit, and unfortunately, we repeatedly felt like we were being pushed toward additional charges rather than receiving straightforward recommendations. On top of that, the wait times were consistently frustrating—usually at least 45 minutes and often over an hour.

The biggest issue was the lack of accountability for the scheduling advice we were given. We trusted their recommendation, followed their instructions, and were then charged because of the outcome. After this experience, we will not be returning.
